summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 5.2/50)

data.turoyo: <...> walḥasəl azzən mqabəl diḏe mzaraṭṭe aʕle w hǧəmme aʕle w kəmzaʕrile kəmzaʕwəqi aʕle <...>
data.translation: <...> Schließlich zogen sie ihm entgegen, sie beleidigten ihn, sie griffen ihn an und beschimpften ihn, schrien ihn an. <...>

rationale: New Infectum box: plural k-form of the expanded -w- root, with directed shouting; no need to borrow a box from zʕq III.

data.turoyo: <...> mzaʕwaqle mə gawe du gubo ʕal as səsye, komər as səsye kalən, hadini a tre.
data.translation: <...> Da schrie er aus dem Innern der Zisterne heraus die Pferde an, da hielten die Pferde inne, beide beruhigten sich.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: masculine shouter, spatial source and explicit ʕal-target.

data.turoyo: Saliqo Manǧe lu quṣro, mžaʕwaqla. Rustam raxu ʕal i səsto w azze lu tarʕo du quṣro.
data.translation: Mändsche stieg oben auf die Burg hinauf und schrie, um Hilfe. Da bestieg Küstern sein Pferd und ritt dicht vor das Burgtor.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: full feminine ž-variant context and edition translation, unlike the inherited isolated mžaʕwaqla form citation.

data.turoyo: Aṯyo li kačke, ftəḥla fema, haṯi i kačke əmmo: “Aṯto no.” Šamiʕo i xatune mi awda, əmmo: “Ṭri mena” - məlla li Piraboke, mzaʕwaqlala li xatune.
data.translation: Als das Mädchen herankam, öffnete sie ihr Maul, um es zu fressen; aber das Mädchen rief: »Ich bin ein Weib«. Wie die Schlossfrau von ihrem Zimmer aus dies hörte, schrie sie der Pîr Abôke zu: »Lass von ihr ab!«

rationale: Thin Preterit cell, reaching five input items: -lala form, direct command, and postposed l-marked speaker; segmentation queried.

summary: The expanded mzaʕwaq-/mzaʕwəq- form supports the inherited zʕwq I filing. Initial m- is not a reason to call it II; related zʕq III is a distinct existing filing.
JTM 5.2/50 supplies the absent Infectum box with plural kəmzaʕwəqi. Preterit has masculine -le, feminine -la and probable agent/recipient -lala; source ž versus z is retained.

Shouting may be undirected or aimed at animals/people with ʕal-. PrS 25/11 adds a recipient suffix and explicit quoted instruction. These frames remain ordinary schreien, with directed shouting described in notes rather than split into an unsupported sense.

PrS 8/11 exactly matches the existing mahzamle. mzaʕwaqla quotation under prs 18/32 and is not added again. PrS 16/39 supplies a usable translated context for the ž-variant already cited as a bare form; its older page-based reference is not silently replaced.
The Infinitiv zəʕwoqo item is only a grammar-page form citation. No new textual Infinitiv evidence or noncompositional idiom is supplied.
At PrS 25/11 does -lala comprise feminine agent plus feminine recipient, with li xatune a postposed l-agent? Retain the printed form until its segmentation is confirmed.

Reconcile existing prs 18/32 with supplied PrS 8/11 and bare mžaʕwaqla at prs 37/3 with PrS 16/39. If the latter is the same verse in page numbering, integrate its new full context with the old bare item rather than count two attestations.
Is z/ž in mzaʕwaq-/mžaʕwaq- dialectal or transcriptional, and what distinction is intended between zʕwq I and related zʕq III?
Can a contextual zəʕwoqo be supplied to supplement the isolated grammar-page Infinitiv citation?
Directed shouting with ʕal-horses and a human ʕal-target retains ordinary schreien; animals are additional addressees, not a new lexical sense.
